questions.question: What is the penalty for fleeing to avoid arrest?

options.text: The driver can be charged with a misdemeanor or felony.
The driver's license can be revoked.

questions.explanation: Fleeing from police is a crime. If you flee from a misdemeanor, it is a misdemeanor. If you flee from a felony, it is a felony. Your license can also be revoked.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is being dangerous, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact. Do not make rude gestures. Put distance between you and the other car.

questions.question: Using a handheld phone while driving is a secondary offense when you use it to:

options.text: Read, type, or send text messages.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read, type, or send text messages.
questions.explanation: Using a handheld phone to read, type, or send text messages while driving is a secondary offense. The fine is $200 to $500.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting in anger, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay away from angry drivers. Do not make eye contact. Do not make gestures that could upset them. Slow down, move over, and do whatever is safe to get away from them.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Stops the seat belt warning light from coming on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should be snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit a fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of their way.
Stop and block them from passing.
Move to the side to give them a clear path.
Signal them when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the side to give them a clear path.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, give them a clear path. Pull to the side of the road if it is safe.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Move into a lane at least one lane away from it, if possible.
Pull onto the left shoulder and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into a lane at least one lane away from it, if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, move into a lane at least one lane away if it is safe. If you cannot change lanes, slow down and pass safely.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: The safest thing to do with an aggressive driver is to get out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers.

questions.question: Children under age six must be in a car seat. Not using one costs $25 and adds one point to your record.
questions.explanation: Children up to age six must be in an approved car seat. Not following this law costs $25 plus court costs and one point on your driving record.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle uses sirens and flashing lights, you should pull to the right side of the road and wait for it to pass.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens, pull to the right side of the road right away and let it pass.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: It weakens the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
It strengthens the effects of both drugs and alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: It strengthens the effects of both drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs makes both substances stronger in your body. Driving after alcohol or drugs is dangerous. Driving after using both together is even more dangerous.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other things?

options.text: The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.explanation: Being tired and being drunk affect your driving in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours damages your driving like having a 0.05% blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours straight damages your driving like having a 0.10% blood alcohol level.

questions.question: Are barricades, vertical panels, drums, and cones commonly used to guide drivers through work zones?
questions.explanation: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, and cones guide drivers safely through work zones. You must drive carefully when passing through a work zone.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, roadwork vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. During the day it looks like an orange triangle. At night it looks like a hollow red triangle.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first. Once the road is clear and you have the right signal, you can complete your turn.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile they travel. You must focus fully on driving. Any other activity can distract you and create danger.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive when conditions are perfect. It is safest to match the speed of other traffic, up to the speed limit. All drivers must drive safely at all times.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a curve is coming.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, go to the nearest rest stop or service area. Take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Do not rely on caffeine pills or energy drinks. They are not a substitute for real rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, how can you ensure safe driving?

options.text: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to arrange a ride with a friend who does not drink. Coffee or cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol or reduce alcohol's effects. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: When should you slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, where you see pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: The most common mistake drivers make when backing up is failing to look both ways behind them.
questions.explanation: The most common backing mistake is not looking both ways behind you. Mirrors do not show everything. Turn your body and head to the right and look through the rear window to see more.

questions.question: What should a driver watch?

options.text: Only directly in front of the car.
Only the middle of the road.
Beside, ahead, and behind the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beside, ahead, and behind the car.
questions.explanation: Watch beside, ahead, and behind your car. Good drivers know what is happening all around their vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.explanation: Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. If one side has a solid line and the other has a broken line, only the side with the broken line can pass. When both sides are solid, no one can pass.
